name: manchester_rx
description: Manchester receive (IEEE 802.3: a 1 is low then high), 20 clocks per bit on in0 (uio5), idle high. Each frame is a sync 1 then 8 data bits LSB first, so it begins with a falling edge at a bit boundary: that edge starts timer0 and the coded shifter. timer0 ticks every half bit (10 clocks) and resyncs on every falling edge, which always lies on a half-bit boundary; the shifter keeps each first half and takes the bit from the second, flagging equal halves as a code violation (status bit 6). Each byte is pushed with a tag byte.
notes: sample_first and sample_phase are the bit's centre clock, (period - 1) // 2 after the edge; the compiler subtracts the contract's edge-to-sample offset (lane_core.edge_to_sample_cycles, measured by the RTL lane-core test) to get the timer counts.
